title: Pods - MCP Memory Server
short: Cross-platform MCP memory server for AI agents. SQLite + FTS5. Stage 1 done, Stage 2 (hosted) next.
content:
## What

A memory server for AI agents. You store things you want the AI to remember across sessions. Pods, I call them. Each pod has a title, content, category, project, session. You can search them with full-text search.

## Why

Every time I talked to an AI I had to repeat context. What am I working on, what decisions were made, what is the architecture. That gets old fast. Pods is the fix.

## How it works

```
You (Claude/OpenCode) -> MCP protocol -> Pods server -> SQLite + FTS5
```

Stage 1 is done. It runs locally, connects to Claude Web via HTTP and OpenCode via stdio. The tools are simple: find, add, get, update, delete, ping.

## Schema (the interesting part)

```sql
CREATE TABLE pods (
  id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  title       TEXT NOT NULL,
  content     TEXT NOT NULL,
  category    TEXT,
  project     TEXT,
  session     TEXT,
  created_at  TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  updated_at  TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  deleted_at  TEXT
);

CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE pods_fts USING fts5(
  title, content, category, project,
  content='pods', content_rowid='rowid'
);
```

## What is left

Stage 2 is hosted. Deploy it somewhere public so pods are accessible from anywhere. The open problem is access control. If an agent can write pods, it can write garbage. Still thinking through that.

> [!note]
> Currently the system that connects is MCP server, however it is not supported in all platforms, so solutions are being thought of to work with platforms that don't provide MCP support like Gemini Web & DeepSeek Web.

[View on GitHub](https://github.com/ch-arslanahmad/pods)

title: Bolt Launcher
short: App launcher (C++/Python). Modular GUI, swap the frontend without touching the backend.
content:
## What

A desktop app launcher for Linux. The idea is simple: keep the backend (search, indexing) separate from the GUI so you can swap either side without touching the other.

## Why

Existing launchers tie the UI and the search together. Want a different look? Too bad. Bolt decouples them. The backend is C++, the GUI is Python/GTK4. They talk over JSON.

## How it is built

- C++ backend handles app detection, indexing, fuzzy search
- Python/GTK4 frontend handles the UI
- Communication over stdin/stdout with JSON
- SQLite for caching

The core works. It reads `.desktop` files, indexes them, searches fast. Wayland native (GTK4 Layer Shell for Hyprland, gsettings for GNOME).

## Why it is shelved

It works but the plugin system is half done. I wanted a system where anyone could write a plugin in any language. That part is not finished. I will pick it up again when I have the time.

[View on GitHub](https://github.com/ch-arslanahmad/bolt-launcher)
